rationale: The recurring method is stated plainly on About and can be reconstructed across three independently supported project contexts. Organizers' vocabulary becomes WOWList's model and publishing workflow; participation and residency needs become documented hosting and access handoffs; coalition listening and public-source relationships become campaign interfaces and recoverable operating memory. These are usable social and information structures with evidence of real use and continuity. The portfolio also shows how an explicit correction changed its own public records, while keeping proposed research and protected coursework distinct from demonstrated delivery.

evidence.finding: The method is explicit: observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people and document enough for others to continue. The project comparisons name relationships, model, interface/use and learning/continuity, with linked evidence. An explicit limit says the pattern does not prove structural equivalence.

Actually followed home to About to WOWList at desktop and mobile. About is one page transition from home and the project two. Opening the mobile menu adds one interaction; the method itself is reached within two interactions.

Decision/action, inspectable artifact and usable result connect the method to technical project management. The current Red Hook example distinguishes delivered audio and a checked print proof from installation. The public-evidence boundary explicitly identifies missing proof rather than filling it in.

A further dated example maps the January 2016 event and later dataset release to independent issue pathways, the original interface, public implementation and documentation. Attributable Council-account interactions are described as public engagement, without claiming formal resident research or official adoption. Archived and unofficial status is visible.

The CallNYC date correction gives a concrete recursive trace: recovered evidence changed the date to 2016 and propagated it to index, case study and resume. Proposed teammate acceptance tests are plainly proposals. The graph practice is not presented as production SaaS, proven client adoption or automated trust.

The protected 2006 coursework claim remains held with no active website surfaces. Its canonical anti-claims reject disciplinary invention, peer-reviewed status, production deployment, sole group authorship and present Max/Jitter proficiency. The public source note withholds faculty testimonials. The separately public Maven certificate is bounded as professional development.

limits: Supported dated past and present projects count under the stated user interpretation. Historical practice is not evidence of current deployment or current proficiency in a historical toolset.

The sequences are source-grounded editorial reconstructions. The review does not infer a formal usability-study protocol, complete iteration log or identical development lifecycle across all projects.

Private source bodies, collaborator communications and participant records were not opened. Their public-safe canonical support and restrictions were inspected; those summaries are not an independent audit of the private source bytes.
CallNYC's public interactions are not proof that residents successfully resolved service needs. The proposed Knowledge Wiki pilot is not counted as completed client adoption.
Only the nine assigned routes and 1280/375 widths were reviewed. Aggregate judge requirements and the separate full QA/release process remain unassessed.
